items.evidence: "Speaker 3 announced the relocation to a larger space on the sixth floor of the Unimile building" plus layout description of one/two/three-person rooms, views, bathrooms, courtyard.

Notes give 15 persons for ~18 slots and mention the lounge/reading room, but do not state the question of whether per-room counts are strict, nor that Susan questioned whether a lounge is needed (notes call it "a significant requirement").

Furniture and equipment constraints covered ("corner desk, chair, filing cabinet... hanging shelves", "photocopier, printer, and fax machine"); the question of what happens if the group does not get the space is missing.
"Speaker 3, Speaker 1, Speaker 2, and Speaker 4 debated several methods for organizing the staff within the available rooms."

Covers project vs professor/assistant grouping, phone calls, partitioning with walls, visitors/overflow, Gisella and admin space. Missing smoking discussion and the meeting room for project members to converge.
Notes never mention the cafeteria or coffee machines.
"Speaker 3 will investigate if rooms can be partitioned with walls or doors to increase privacy."
Nothing about finding out whether Gisella can be placed with the school's other admin.
Only implied by "to review concrete proposals from participants"; not stated that each member comes up with their own preferences.
"Members were tasked with consulting colleagues, such as Maggie and Pierrette, to gather their preferences before the next meeting."
"before a final proposal can be drafted" is vague; not stated as a team task to build one coherent proposal.
Notes mention "negotiation with other groups" and that another group is working on a solution, but not that the proposals will be merged.
Maggie and Pierrette are mentioned as people to consult, but no owner is given (Susan volunteered to ask them).
"The next meeting is scheduled for next Tuesday at 2:00 PM"
Notes say "There is uncertainty regarding whether grouping should be based on specific projects or by professional roles"; transcript shows the group rejected grouping by project (D and C: "No").

Notes: "participants discussed if she should occupy a one-person room or share a larger space with an overflow/visitor slot." Transcript shows this was proposed but D objected that senior visitors cannot sit in the admin office, so it was not firmly decided; notes reflect the option but not as a decision.
No mention that there is no cafeteria.
"Is it feasible to fit four people into a three-person room through intelligent desk arrangement?"
Notes discuss gathering individual preferences, phone/confidentiality needs, and consulting Maggie and Pierrette.
"whether grouping should be based on specific projects or by professional roles such as professor and assistant."
"Can rooms be partitioned with walls and new doors to provide more privacy?" (cubicles not mentioned).
Notes ask whether the lounge should be a reading room or meeting/overflow space, but not whether a lounge is needed at all.
Visitors appear only as an overflow use of the lounge and a visitor slot with Gisella; the lack of room for growth/visitors is not stated as a problem.
"A significant concern was raised regarding Gisela, whose administrative role involves high noise levels"
"The group addressed the challenge of accommodating administrative staff like Gisella in the new layout."
Cafeteria not mentioned.
Coffee machines not mentioned.

errors.claim: The group considered whether professors should share offices with their assistants, noting this is common in other faculties but not necessarily here.
errors.why_wrong: Reversed: Andre said professors at this school commonly share with assistants; Susan said in every other faculty professors have their own offices.

errors.claim: There is uncertainty regarding whether grouping should be based on specific projects or by professional roles such as professor and assistant.
errors.why_wrong: The group answered this: D and C rejected grouping by project because projects change and people work on several; it was not left uncertain.

errors.claim: A significant requirement discussed is the creation of a lounge or reading room to serve as a meeting or overflow space.
errors.why_wrong: The lounge's use as meeting/overflow space was explicitly called an open discussion with no decision; Susan even questioned whether a lounge is needed.
